=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- File: tools/repo_tree/update_repo_tree.py
Line or code reference: parse_marker_spans() — MARKER_PATTERN.fullmatch() around line 186
Problem: When a malformed marker line (e.g. `<!-- TREE:START id=.invalid -->`) fails the MARKER_PATTERN regex, parse_marker_spans silently treats it as ordinary content. The eventual error ("missing TREE marker pair(s)") does not point to the malformed line that is actually present in the file.
Why it fails at runtime: An operator who mistypes a marker id in agents.md receives a misleading "missing marker pair" error with no pointer to the line they actually need to fix. load_config validates marker_id syntax early for the config entries themselves, but the file-side parse path silently drops invalid markers instead of flagging them.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: tools/repo_tree/update_repo_tree.py
Line or code reference: load_config() — validation error calls to fail() near lines 111-145
Problem: Config validation errors (non-string/empty field, absolute-path guard, path-traversal guard, marker_id character check) use the default exit code EXIT_DIFF (1) via fail(), while only the duplicate-config-entry guard explicitly passes exit_code=EXIT_MARKER_ERROR (2).
Why it fails at runtime: Callers that distinguish between exit code 1 (drift — regenerate needed) and exit code 2 (malformed markers — hard input failure) will misclassify an invalid config as a simple "needs regeneration" case rather than an input validation error. The duplicate-entry guard in load_config correctly sets exit_code=EXIT_MARKER_ERROR, but the other validation errors do not.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Requirement: "Run make generate and then make generate-check; both tree blocks in agents.md should round-trip cleanly." — the linked issue specifies this as a validation step, and the Makefile contract already wires these commands.
Expected change site: .github/workflows/ci.yml (test allowlist section)
Evidence of absence: The ci.yml workflow runs Python tests via explicit per-file invocations (e.g. `python3 tests/test_ci_inventory_parity_order_contract.py`, `python3 tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`, etc.) and does not use --discover or a glob pattern. Grep of .github/workflows/ci.yml shows no reference to test_update_repo_tree.py. The new test will execute locally when invoked directly but will never run in CI, leaving the repo-tree marker logic without automated gate protection.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- File: tools/repo_tree/update_repo_tree.py  
Line or code reference: load_config:150 (MARKER_ID_PATTERN.fullmatch) + parse_marker_spans:186  
Problem: The tightened regex still accepts marker_ids containing `.` or `-` in positions that can lead to ambiguous HTML-comment parsing (e.g. IDs starting/ending with `.` or containing consecutive delimiters).  
Why it fails at runtime: A malformed ID in config.yaml or agents.md produces either a silent skip (treated as content) or a generic "missing marker pair" error instead of the specific EXIT_MARKER_ERROR=2 path; downstream CI/make targets misclassify the failure.  
SEVERITY: MAJOR  
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: tools/repo_tree/update_repo_tree.py  
Line or code reference: expand_source_glob:153 (`sorted(set(matches))`)  
Problem: Even with `path.is_file()` (good fix from previous pass), `set()` + `sorted()` on glob output can still be unstable across Python versions or filesystem enumeration order when a glob matches many similarly-named files.  
Why it fails at runtime: Rendered blocks in agents.md can differ on successive `make generate` runs, triggering spurious `make generate-check` failures and CI flakes.  
SEVERITY: MAJOR  
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: tools/repo_tree/update_repo_tree.py  
Line or code reference: load_config:84-109 (all `raise fail(...)` branches) + main:310 (RepoTreeError handler)  
Problem: Most config/validation errors (invalid YAML, missing file, bad marker_id, duplicate tree entry) emit `::error::FAIL: ...` but use default `exit_code=1` (drift) instead of the documented `EXIT_MARKER_ERROR=2` for malformed-marker cases.  
Why it fails at runtime: Scripts that branch on exit code (e.g. Makefile, CI) cannot reliably distinguish "needs regeneration" from "hard input error", and error messages lack file:line context for the offending config entry.  
SEVERITY: NIT
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
